summary: SPIKE: Astro 7 storefront shell — prove or reject ADR-006
description:
Timeboxed spike (2 days) with a throwaway prototype — no production code, no scaffold dependency. Decides the storefront shell framework (Astro 7 + React islands vs React SPA) before US-002 (TKT-26) builds storefront UI. Outcome = ADR-006 moved from Proposed to Accepted or Rejected, with evidence.

**Priority:** P1   **Depends on:** — (independent; blocks TKT-26)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Prototype: event list + event detail in Astro 7 — page HTML cached at the ADR-004 minutes tier, availability as a React island polling the seconds tier, Cache-Control set per route class via src/fetch.ts
- [ ] Buy-half seam test: hold-countdown state survives MPA navigation into a React checkout surface; seams documented honestly, including what breaks
- [ ] FR/EN locale routing demonstrated on localized event content (TKT-36 shape)
- [ ] Written caching ownership rule (page layer vs API layer per ADR-004 tier) resolving the TKT-31 overlap — stale-page/fresh-API mismatch impossible by construction
- [ ] Early-adopter tax log: compiler strictness, Rolldown/plugin gaps, bugs hit during the spike, with a tolerable/not-tolerable judgment
- [ ] ADR-006 completed (Accepted or Rejected) from the evidence; report posted on this ticket

Quality gates: n/a (throwaway prototype); the deliverable is the report + the ADR decision.

binding.rule: We adopt Go for all backend services and TypeScript + React for the three frontends (storefront, back office, scanner). Money is represented as integer minor units + ISO currency code everywhere; floats are banned on money paths.

Every public read endpoint declares a volatility-tiered TTL with explicit Cache-Control (seat maps: hours; event lists/detail: minutes; price display: ~1 min; availability: seconds; hold/order/scan state: never cached); hot events are served from in-memory structures refreshed/invalidated from the write path; frontends make few aggregated calls and refresh on the endpoint's TTL cadence; writes are never cached.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
## Execution plan — Astro 7 storefront spike (throwaway)

**Grounding (verified in-repo, not assumed):**
- `services/catalog/cmd/catalog/main.go` is a **skeleton**: "No domain routes yet — those arrive with their stories." There is **no** real event-list / event-detail / availability endpoint to wire against. So the spike **stubs the API layer** with a tiny mock that emits ADR-004-tiered `Cache-Control` headers. This keeps the spike true to "no scaffold dependency" and still exercises the real question: does the **page layer** enforce ADR-004 and do the buy-half seams hold.
- `web/storefront/` is a placeholder (`index.html` + nginx) — nothing to preserve or integrate.
- ADR-004 tiers I'll target: event list/detail = **minutes**; availability = **seconds**; price ≈ 1 min; hold/order state = **never**. `src/fetch.ts` sets `Cache-Control`/`s-maxage` **per route class**.

**DoD (maps 1:1 to the 6 ACs):**
1. Astro 7 app: `/[locale]/events` (list) + `/[locale]/events/[slug]` (detail). Page HTML cached at minutes tier; availability rendered by a **React island** polling the seconds-tier stub. `Cache-Control` set per route class in `src/fetch.ts`. **Evidence:** curl -I showing distinct `s-maxage` per route + island network trace via Chrome DevTools.
2. **Buy-half seam test:** hold-countdown state started on the detail page must survive MPA nav into a React checkout surface. I'll implement the honest cross-MPA mechanism (persist hold deadline to `sessionStorage`/URL, rehydrate in the checkout island) and **document what breaks** (e.g. in-memory React state is lost across MPA nav; timer drift; back-button restore). This AC passes on *honest documentation*, not on zero breakage.
3. **FR/EN locale routing** on localized event content (TKT-36 shape) — `/fr/...` vs `/en/...`, localized title/description from the stub.
4. **Caching-ownership rule** (resolves TKT-31 overlap): a written rule assigning each ADR-004 tier to exactly one layer (page vs API) so a stale-page/fresh-API mismatch is **impossible by construction** — e.g. "page layer owns minutes-tier HTML; API layer owns seconds-tier availability; the page never embeds availability in cached HTML, only the island fetches it." Goes into ADR-006 + the report.
5. **Early-adopter-tax log:** compiler strictness, Rolldown/Vite 8 + plugin gaps, Sätteri, actual bugs hit — each with a tolerable / not-tolerable call.
6. **ADR-006 decision:** Accept (Option 1) iff ACs 1–4 hold and 5 is tolerable; else Reject, Option 2 stands. Report posted on this ticket.

**Where it lives:** `spike/astro7/` inside the worktree, **gitignored** (throwaway). Only committed artifacts: the report (`docs/` or ticket comment) + the ADR-006 status flip. No production code, no scaffold dep.

**Test seam:** n/a for shippable tests (throwaway prototype, per the ticket's "Quality gates: n/a"). "Tests" here = reproducible evidence: `curl -I` header captures + a DevTools network trace for the island poll + a written seam walk-through. `make check` is not run against spike code (it's gitignored and not part of the gate).

**Steps:** (a) scaffold Astro 7 in `spike/astro7`, pin exact version; (b) stub API with tiered headers; (c) build list+detail with availability island; (d) `src/fetch.ts` per-route `Cache-Control`; (e) locale routing; (f) hold-countdown → checkout seam + honest write-up; (g) capture evidence; (h) write ownership rule; (i) tax log; (j) fill ADR-006 + post report.

**Pre-mortem (how this spike fails):**
- *False positive:* stub is so friendly it hides real integration cost → mitigate by giving the stub the **real ADR-004 header contract**, not a convenient one.
- *AC-2 hand-waved:* "state survives" claimed without showing the break modes → I commit to documenting at least the failure cases, per the AC's own wording.
- *Astro 7 too fresh to install:* Rolldown/plugin breakage blocks scaffold → that **is** signal (AC-5); I log it and, if fatal, Reject with evidence rather than forcing it.
- *Timebox:* 2 days. If AC 1–4 aren't cleanly met within the box, the decision is **Reject** (Option 2 stands) — a spike that can't prove the gains in the box has answered the question.

**risk:low rationale (challenged):** zero production code, gitignored, isolated, no auth/data/CI/deploy surface, ≤ a handful of committed files (report + ADR edit). Stands. Plan gate skipped per invariant; proceeding to codex plan-review then building.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
## Plan revised after codex cross-model critique

Codex critique was strong; incorporated in full. **Net change: the spike gets harder to fool.** Revisions:

**1. Prove cache _behavior_, not just emitted headers (AC1).** Not enough that `src/fetch.ts` emits an `s-maxage` — I embed a **mock revision marker + timestamp** in each response and show two sequential requests where the **minutes-tier page HTML is reused** (same marker) while the **seconds-tier availability island keeps getting a fresh marker**. That's the mismatch-by-construction claim demonstrated, not asserted.

**2. Per-surface header dumps (AC1).** Separate `curl -I` captures for: list HTML, detail HTML, availability API, and a hold/order endpoint — the last must be `no-store`/`no-cache` (transactional, ADR-004 "never cached"). Price display gets its own **~1-min tier** capture (codex flagged I'd dropped it).

**3. AC2 = a real React SPA checkout route, adversarially tested.** Boundary defined: Astro MPA detail → a `/checkout` route hosting a **React SPA root** (not just a component). I test: reload, back/forward, duplicate tab, **expired hold**, missing/corrupt storage, **direct checkout URL with no prior hold**, and **storage-disabled**. Security: persist only an **opaque hold ID + deadline**, never a bearer-like token in the URL (history/referrer/log leak). Each case gets a pass / breaks-thus writeup — honest seams are the AC.

**4. AC3 — locale is end-to-end, not route-matching.** Localized content + locale **preserved through internal links and into checkout**, invalid/default-locale fallback, and locale-aware formatting (dates/money display).

**5. AC4 — encode the invariant, don't just narrate it.** The ownership rule is demonstrated structurally: **minutes-tier page HTML contains zero volatile availability**; availability exists **only** behind the seconds-tier client endpoint the island calls; price lives at its own ~1-min tier. Because cached HTML physically cannot carry availability, stale-page/fresh-API mismatch is impossible by construction — shown, then written as the rule.

**6. AC5 — fixed tax-log schema:** `issue | workaround | elapsed | upstream status | production consequence`, plus a per-row tolerable/not call. Prevents "tolerable" becoming hindsight.

**7. Biggest risk = FALSE ACCEPT from an in-process mock (codex's lead finding).** A too-friendly in-process mock bypasses gateway routing, cross-origin/cookie behavior, CDN/proxy interpretation of `s-maxage`, SSR deploy mode, timeouts/errors, and real hold semantics — Astro could look clean only because the mock is shaped for it. Mitigation: **run the mock as a separate HTTP origin behind a gateway-shaped reverse proxy** (nginx, mirroring the repo's storefront nginx), and **inject latency, 5xx, changing ETags, and expired holds**. ADR-006 will state explicitly: acceptance means **"shell hypothesis supported," not "integration proven,"** and will **list the untested integration costs** as follow-ups (gateway wiring, CDN adapter, generated API contract, real hold identity).

**8. Guard against FALSE REJECT.** The tax log **separates framework/architecture blockers from environment/setup/install failures** (Rolldown install flakiness ≠ Astro-the-architecture failing). Only architecture blockers count against Accept.

**Timebox discipline (codex):** deliberately narrow — one list route, one detail route, one availability island, one checkout transition. No generalized mock infra, no production testing. Day 1: scaffold + HTTP mock + cache experiment. Day 2: state seam + evidence + decision. If ACs 1–4 aren't cleanly met in the box → Reject, Option 2 stands.

Proceeding to build (risk:low → no plan gate).

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
**Prototype built + evidence captured; PR #4 open.**

Built (throwaway, gitignored `spike/`): Node mock API with ADR-004-tiered `Cache-Control` + fault injection, an nginx gateway (captured through real nginx 1.27), and an Astro 7.0.7 SSR app (list/detail + availability React island + hold-countdown → React SPA checkout + i18n middleware). Delegated the mechanical build to gpt-5.5/codex; drove verification myself (codex sandbox can't open TCP listeners).

**Verified in a real browser through real nginx** (`spike/EVIDENCE.md`): per-surface cache tiers (minutes HTML / seconds availability / `no-store` transactional), availability provably absent from cached HTML, hold-countdown surviving MPA nav into the React checkout (115s→111s, no reset), and all 5 checkout failure states (valid/expired/missing/corrupt/storage-disabled). Money is integer minor units + ISO currency (ADR-001).

Committed deliverables only: spike report (`docs/spikes/`), ADR-006 flipped to Accepted with fictional API names corrected to real `astro@7.0.7`, and `.gitignore`. Next: codex adversarial review of the diff.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
**Codex adversarial review — 3 blocking findings, all valid. Fixing, not defending.**

1. **AC4 "impossible by construction" was overstated (BLOCKING).** True only for *availability* (structurally absent from HTML). I wrongly generalized it, then **embedded price into cached HTML while ALSO exposing an independently-cached price API** — two copies of one value with independent cache lifetimes = a real stale-page/fresh-API mismatch. Since ADR-006's rule makes AC4 failure → Reject, I can't Accept on the old wording.
2. **Page caching was asserted, not demonstrated (BLOCKING).** The spike nginx was a pass-through proxy with no `proxy_cache`; I proved header *emission*, not cache *reuse*.
3. **"Every failure state handled" overclaimed (BLOCKING).** One of five is the happy path; more materially, checkout trusts the stored deadline and never re-validates against `GET /api/holds/:id` — a server-revoked hold with a future client deadline renders "valid". That's a seam demo, not rehydration *correctness*.
+ incidental: ADR body still literally names the fictional `src/fetch.ts`/`Astro.cache`.

**Fixes in progress:** (a) close the price double-source so AC4's guarantee is real (single-source: price lives only in the page, no independently-cached price endpoint on the browse path); (b) add nginx `proxy_cache` and demonstrate actual HTML reuse + availability bypass; (c) add server-side hold re-validation on checkout rehydration and downgrade the claim wording; (d) correct the ADR body, not just a preamble. Then re-green evidence and re-post.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
**Codex review triaged — 3 blocking findings all fixed & verified. → needs:human (Gate 3).**

| Finding | Verdict | Fix (verified) |
|---|---|---|
| AC4 "impossible by construction" overstated; price double-source | blocking, valid | One aggregated page read carries price; standalone `/price` → `no-store`. Ownership rule rewritten with an explicit **single-source** clause. Re-tested: only the page is a cacheable price copy. |
| Page caching asserted, not demonstrated | blocking, valid | nginx `proxy_cache` added; evidence now shows real HTML reuse `X-Cache-Status: MISS`→`HIT`, not header emission. |
| Checkout trusts client deadline | blocking, valid | Checkout re-validates against `GET /api/holds/:id`; forged future-deadline hold now renders "no longer valid" (verified in-browser). |
| ADR body still names fictional APIs | incidental, valid | Corrected the ADR **body** (Context + AC1 + References), not just the preamble. |
| integer-money / availability-absence | (review confirmed correct) | no change needed |

Followed the "fix in PR, don't re-run codex on my own fixes" rule; fixes verified by clean Astro build + real-browser re-test through real nginx. **Decision stays ACCEPT** — the four gating criteria are now genuinely met, honestly scoped ("shell hypothesis proven, not integration").

**Ball is with the human (Gate 3):** review PR #4 and, if good, **squash-merge** in the repo, then move TKT-39 → PO Review. Review-guide posted on the PR. Note: this is a spike — the merged artifacts are the report + ADR decision only; the prototype is throwaway/gitignored.
